title: Can a Chess Player Solve a MURDER?
not_playable_reason: Not chess: the narrator solves two Murdle logic-deduction murder-mystery puzzles (daily mini + full daily puzzle); suspects are mapped to chess.com bot portraits as a joke.
summary: Break from variants: the narrator solves Murdle puzzles (murdle.com, Aug 28 daily mini 'no longer living freshman Logician' and the full daily 'cup of poisoned tea' art-museum case). Each puzzle lists suspects, weapons and locations; each suspect has exactly one unique weapon and location; clues (fingerprint matching, reversed-word coded messages, statements) let you fill a deduction grid with X/checks and accuse the murderer with weapon and place. He gets both right (Father Mango w/ heavy backpack in the parking lot; Chef Aubergine w/ rare vase in the bathroom).
rules: Murdle-style logic grid: N suspects x N weapons x N locations (3 for mini, 5 for daily); each suspect pairs with one unique weapon and one unique location.

Clues: fingerprint image comparison, coded messages (reversed words / scrambled letters), statements like 'X never set foot on the quad', 'Y was flirting with the person who had the sharp pencil', 'a heavy backpack was used'.
Player marks the grid, then accuses: who, with what, where.
win_condition: Correct accusation of murderer + weapon + location.

opponent.name: none (puzzle)

setup: Mini: suspects Father Mango, President Amaranth, Miss Saffron; weapons heavy backpack, poisoned apple, sharp pencil; locations parking lot, quad, campus observatory. Daily: suspects Agent Fuchsia, Brother Brownstone, Baron Maroon, Chef Aubergine, Admiral Navy; weapons poisoned wine, rare vase, abstract statue, cup of poisoned tea, heavy painting; locations art studio, gift shop, rooftop garden, bathroom, entry hall.
current_impl_issues: Legacy 'murder' (Whodunit: one bot piece is secretly the murderer; capture it) is an invented chess variant; the video has no chess. If kept, label as inspired-by, or implement a small Murdle-style deduction mini-game with chess-bot suspects.
